subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or should Slack setup/default behavior change beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured gap is mostly before OpenClaw code runs, but steering or changing defaults affects Slack setup expectations, public-ingress requirements, and upgrade/operator guidance.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and make the Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing deployment-shape transport table is sufficient and close only after that maintainer decision is explicit.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and make the Slack docs/setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the recent measurement/fix trail and explicitly scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP mode guidance.
